The Apostle Paul alerts the Galatians to the importance of generosity in giving, and even warns them against neglecting God's commandments by honoring the teachers and meeting their needs (Lk 10:7). What man offers of love to the teachers he will reap as happiness in heaven, based on the rule known among farmers, that whoever sows a good kind reaps good fruits, and the opposite is also true.

entries.section: (3) Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap

paragraphs.text: Paul confirms the meaning mentioned in the previous verse, that whoever refuses to give the teachers their material needs because he is busy with his fleshly lusts and selfishness will receive nothing, for the flesh will become dust and all the material lusts will pass away; indeed eternal torment awaits him because of his absorption in his lusts. But whoever cares for the spiritual work and for giving will be rewarded with glories in eternal life.

entries.section: (3) Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul encourages us to continue to care for meeting the needs of the teachers and to do every good and mercy, and to persevere in that, because the complete result will appear in eternal life. For God in due season will bless us in part on earth so that we continue doing good, and fully in heaven so that we enjoy it forever.

entries.section: (3) Whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap

paragraphs.text: Paul considers doing good an opportunity that the spiritual man should seize, so that he shows his love for God and for others and lays up for himself a treasure in heaven, and does good to every man, and especially to the believers, because he is more in contact with them and responsible for them; they are members with him in one body, which is the Church, while the unbelievers may find their needs met from others. His love and giving are for all, but he begins with the believers.

Doing good by helping others is a blessing to you before it is to the other. So do not turn away the one who asks you for something, especially if you are sure of his need; rather, would that you strive to provide for the needs of others, and care for those close to you, that is, your household and relatives and all those you live with, because you are responsible for them before God, not only in material things but rather in spiritual things, that is, the salvation of their souls and their attachment to the Church.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: The Apostle Paul was accustomed to dictate his epistles to one of his helpers and then write a greeting at the end, or a signature, to confirm that he was the sender of the epistle. In the Epistle to the Galatians, however, he wrote the whole epistle or a large part of it with his own hand, and he wrote it in large letters because of his weak eyesight. His care for this epistle shows his emphasis on its meanings and its importance, and he asks those to whom he sent it to hold to it.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: Paul speaks about the false teachers, who are Christians of Jewish origin and proclaim the necessity of circumcision to receive salvation. By this they please the Jews because they have added new members to Judaism, so that the Jews would not persecute them because of their conversion to Christianity, and would consider them concerned for Judaism since they convert the Gentiles to it by circumcision. This, of course, is a great error, because salvation is by the cross and the blood of Christ only and not by circumcision or by anything else.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: The false teachers did not oblige those of the Christians of Gentile origin who were circumcised to the works of the Law, and were content with circumcision, for this meant the joining of the Gentiles to Judaism, so that the anger of the Jews would consequently be kept away from these teachers, since these teachers would be considered preachers of Judaism and not Christians who had left Judaism. They boast that they have circumcised, that is, joined many to Judaism.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: The world is crucified unto me: since Paul believed in the cross, it made him die to fleshly lusts and to all the pride and grandeur of the world, so that he no longer seeks anything of them, for they were crucified to him, that is, died. And I unto the world: on the other hand, he became crucified to the world, that is, ready to bear sufferings and death for the sake of Christ in his preaching and his service to the world, to draw souls to faith.

The Apostle Paul declares his difference from the false teachers and that he does not seek any boasting in the material things of the world or in the opinions and approval of people, but, as an example to us, he boasts in the salvation he received through Christ the Redeemer on the cross.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: Paul declares that salvation is not obtained by the uncircumcised, that is, the Gentiles, nor by the circumcised, that is, the Jews, but by the new creation, that is, those born again in the font of Baptism, who receive the new nature by which they live with God.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: The Israel of God: what is meant is the Christian people.

Paul affirms the blessings granted to whoever lives by this sound thought, that is, faith in Christ the Savior, receiving Baptism, and not caring about circumcision. These blessings, which he expresses as God's grace and mercy, include all the believers among the Christians, for they are the new Israel who believed in the awaited Messiah, the Savior.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: From henceforth let no man trouble me: no one can cast doubt on my apostleship and my following of Christ.

The marks of the Lord Jesus: the traces of the wounds and torments that Paul bore for Christ. Paul ends his speech by forbidding the Galatians to debate the subject of circumcision, to return to Judaism, and to follow the false teachers in their casting doubt on Paul's apostleship and faithfulness to Christ, and he offers the proof of his following of Christ, which is the marks of the torments visible in his body, which he bore for the sake of Christ. It is not merely a matter of discussions and argument; what matters is that we love Christ, who died for us, and bear everything for His sake.

entries.section: (4) The cross and the new creation

paragraphs.text: Paul concludes his epistle by asking for the grace of God, in whom they believed, to be with their spirits and to bless them.

Control your lusts and bear insults for the sake of Christ, and then you will enjoy the blessings of the cross in your life, of reassurance, strength and joy; indeed, sufferings become a cause of blessing and pride, because they are your way to enjoy the abundant graces of God.
